newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower on rising dollar vs yen.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower on rising dollar vs yen.

text.p: The won ended lower as the dollar gained strength against the yen in world markets, but dealers said the U.S. currency was trapped in a narrow range of 891/892 won throughout Thursday.
After opening at 891.50, the won fell to a low of 892.00 as the dollar rose to 115 yen in Tokyo.
With no follow-through dollar buying, the won finished at 891.30, compared with Wednesday's close of 891.00.
Dealers said the local market seemed generally unaffected by the yen/dollar with a view of more dollar supply on some repayment due for forward trading and exporter deals.
"The 117 yen level looked to be the highest point from a medium-point of view as Japan prefers the dollar to remain at the 110-120 yen mark," said a foreign bank dealer.
A local bank dealer forecast the dollar would test the 890 won level, if it fell against the yen in world markets.
Dealers estimated Thursday's trading volume totalled $1.01 billion. Friday's mid-rate was expected to be pegged at 891.40 against 890.90 today.
